glossario.simples: When people vote to choose who will hold an office.
The election for president, governor, senator and deputies, all on the same day.
The election for mayor and city councilor, who take care of the cities.
Each round of voting. Some elections have two rounds. In Portuguese: {{turno}}.
The document of a person who is registered to vote. In Portuguese: {{título de eleitor}}.
An app from the Electoral Justice that keeps the voter card on a cell phone.
A notice to the Electoral Justice explaining why the person did not vote. In Portuguese: {{justificativa}}.
A vote that the person can choose to cast or not. In Portuguese: {{voto facultativo}}.
The part of the Justice system that organizes elections and takes care of their rules. The TSE is its highest court. In Portuguese: {{Justiça Eleitoral}}.
The machine we vote on. In Portuguese: {{urna eletrônica}}.
The place, usually a school classroom, where a group of voters votes. In Portuguese: {{seção eleitoral}}.
A paper that the voting machine prints at the end of voting, with the votes from that polling station. In Portuguese: {{boletim de urna}}.
A test in which outside experts try to find flaws in the voting machine before the election.
A way of counting votes in which whoever gets the most votes wins.
A way of counting votes in which the seats are divided according to the votes of each party.
A vote given only to the party's number, without choosing a candidate. In Portuguese: {{voto de legenda}}.
The votes given to candidates or to parties. Blank and null votes do not count.
More than half.
How many votes are worth one seat: the valid votes divided by the number of seats. In Portuguese: {{quociente eleitoral}}.
Seats that are still free after the first division among the parties. In Portuguese: {{sobras}}.
A group of people with similar ideas that puts forward candidates.
Parties that join together for at least 4 years and act as one.
A union of parties for just one election. In Portuguese: {{coligação}}.
Someone who cannot be a candidate for a period of time.
A group of judges who decide together.
The candidates' ads asking for votes.
A fake video or audio, made by computer, that imitates a real person.
Artificial intelligence: a computer program that can create texts, images, videos and sounds.
A person who has officially joined a party.
A type of law that gives details on subjects that the Constitution says need more explanation.
A rule written by the TSE (Superior Electoral Court) to organize the elections.

slides.titulo: Elections: the people's turn to choose
slides.texto: In an election, each person votes to **choose** who will decide on behalf of everyone. It is like electing the class representative, only giant-sized.

slides.titulo: There is an election every 2 years
slides.texto: Elections take turns: one year, it is the turn of the country and the states. Two years later, it is the cities' turn.

itens.txt: **General elections**, like the one in 2026: president, governor, senator and deputies.
**Municipal elections**, like the one in 2024: mayor and city councilor.
First round: on the first Sunday of October. In 2026, it was on October 4.
Runoff (second round), when needed: on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, it was on October 25.
Voting runs from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Brasília time.

slides.texto: To vote, a person needs a **voter card** ({{título de eleitor}}).

itens.txt: From age 18, voting is **mandatory**.
People who are 16 or 17, over 70, or cannot read have an optional vote.
The voter card can be kept on a cell phone, in the e-Título app.
People who must vote and did not vote need to justify their absence within 60 days after each round.
If the justification is not accepted, the person pays a fine.

slides.coruja: You can justify your absence in the e-Título app itself, without leaving home.

itens.txt: The vote is **secret**: no one can see who you voted for.
The electronic voting machine ({{urna eletrônica}}) has been used in Brazil since 1996.
At the end of voting, each machine prints the **voting machine report** ({{boletim de urna}}), with the votes from that polling station.
The TSE (Superior Electoral Court) puts the voting machine reports on the internet. Anyone can check them.
Before the election, experts test the voting machine in public to try to find flaws.

slides.coruja: The public security test for the 2026 elections took place from December 1 to 5, 2025.

slides.titulo: Two ways of counting the votes

itens: Whoever gets the most votes wins.
It is used for president, governor, mayor and senator.
Sometimes a runoff (second round) is needed.
colunas.exemplo: Like the election for class representative: the one with the most votes wins.

itens: It is used for deputies and city councilors.
First, the seats are divided among the parties, according to the votes of each one.
Then, the candidates with the most votes in each party get the seats.
You can vote just for the party's number: this is the party vote.
colunas.exemplo: Like dividing the places in a tournament among the classes, according to the size of each class.

slides.texto: It can only happen for president, governor and mayor of a city with more than 200,000 voters.

itens.txt: To win in the first round, a candidate needs **more than half** of the valid votes.
Valid votes are the ones given to candidates. Blank and null votes are left out.
If no one gets there, the 2 candidates with the most votes compete in a runoff.
In the runoff, whoever gets the most valid votes wins.
In a city with up to 200,000 voters, the mayoral candidate with the most votes wins in the first round.

slides.titulo: Simulator: how the seats are divided
slides.texto: A make-believe city is going to elect 10 city councilors. Together, the parties got 1,000 valid votes.
passos: Electoral quota = valid votes ÷ seats. Here: 1,000 ÷ 10 = **100 votes** per seat.
Each party gets 1 seat for every 100 votes: Circle 4, Square 2, Triangle 1 and Diamond 1. That is already 8 seats.
2 seats are left over. They go to the highest averages. The average is: the party's votes ÷ (seats it already has + 1).
1st leftover seat: Circle 420 ÷ 5 = 84. Square 270 ÷ 3 = 90. Triangle 190 ÷ 2 = 95. Diamond 120 ÷ 2 = 60. It goes to Triangle.
2nd leftover seat: Triangle's average drops to 190 ÷ 3 = 63.3. The highest now is Square's (90). It goes to Square.
Result: Circle 4, Square 3, Triangle 2 and Diamond 1. In each party, the candidates with the most votes get the seats.
Extra rule: for the seats from the first division, a candidate needs at least 10% of the quota (here, 10 votes).
For the leftover seats, at first only parties with 80% of the quota and candidates with 20% compete. If there are still seats left, all parties take part, as the STF decided in 2024.

slides.texto: Before the vote, there are rules for people who want to be candidates and for the campaign.

cards.txt: A group of people with similar ideas. In Brazil, you can only run for office through a party.
cards.mais: The Constitution requires every candidate to be a party member (art. 14, § 3).

cards.txt: Two or more parties can join together and act as if they were just one.
cards.mais: A coalition, on the other hand, is a union just for the election. Since 2020, coalitions are not allowed in elections for deputies and city councilors.

cards.txt: The parties ask the Electoral Justice ({{Justiça Eleitoral}}) to register their candidates.
People with certain convictions decided by a group of judges become **ineligible** for 8 years or more.
cards.mais: In 2025, Complementary Law 219 changed how this time is counted. In many cases, the 8 years count from the conviction. In others, the person is ineligible from the conviction until 8 years after serving the sentence.

cards.txt: Election advertising can only start on August 16. On radio and TV, there is free airtime before the election.
cards.mais: Paid political advertising on radio and television is forbidden.

cards.txt: It is forbidden to use false or manipulated content in election advertising, like a **deepfake**. Anything made with AI must be labeled.
cards.mais: These rules are in a TSE resolution (Resolution 23,610/2019). Anyone who breaks them can face the courts.

slides.titulo: What about blank or null votes?
slides.texto: Both are allowed. See what happens to them.

itens.txt: Blank vote: the person presses the BRANCO (blank) key and then confirms.
Null vote: the person types a number that does not belong to any candidate and confirms.
Both are **left out** of the count of valid votes.
They do not cancel the election, even if there are many of them.
An election is only held again by a court decision, when there are problems like fraud.

slides.pergunta: In an election, half of the people voted null. What happens?
opcoes: Null votes do not count, and the result of the valid votes stands
Whoever voted null must vote again
slides.explica: Null votes and blank votes are not counted as valid votes. They do not cancel the election.
